name: Desktop E2E Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to checkout (tag, branch, or SHA)'
        required: false
        type: string

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Detect Changes
    # Only run change detection for push events (skip for workflow_dispatch and workflow_call)
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      desktop: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.desktop }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        id: filter
        with:
          base: ${{ github.event.before }}
          filters: |
            desktop:
              - 'apps/desktop/src/**'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/**'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/vendor/**'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/**'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/resources/**'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs'
              - 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/rust-toolchain.toml'
              - 'apps/desktop/index.html'
              - 'apps/desktop/vite.config.*'
              - 'apps/desktop/tsconfig*'
              - 'packages/crypto/src/**'
              - 'packages/crypto/tsconfig*'
              - '.github/workflows/e2e-desktop.yml'

  e2e-desktop:
    name: Desktop E2E (${{ matrix.platform }})
    needs: [changes]
    if: >-
      always() && !cancelled() &&
      (
        github.event_name != 'push' ||
        needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true'
      )
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: macos
            os: macos-latest
            fuse-feature: fuse
            binary-name: cipherbox-desktop
          - platform: windows
            os: windows-latest
            fuse-feature: winfsp
            binary-name: cipherbox-desktop.exe
          - platform: linux
            os: ubuntu-22.04
            fuse-feature: fuse
            binary-name: cipherbox-desktop

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}

      # --- Install FUSE driver (needed for both build and test) ---

      - name: Install FUSE-T (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install --cask fuse-t
          sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig
          FUSE_T_PC="/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/pkgconfig/fuse-t.pc"
          if [ ! -f "$FUSE_T_PC" ]; then
            FUSE_T_PC=$(find /Library /usr/local /opt/homebrew -name "fuse-t.pc" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
          fi
          if [ -z "$FUSE_T_PC" ] || [ ! -f "$FUSE_T_PC" ]; then
            echo "::error::fuse-t.pc not found after FUSE-T installation"
            exit 1
          fi
          sudo cp "$FUSE_T_PC" /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc
          sudo sed -i '' 's/^Version:.*/Version: 2.9.9/' /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc

      - name: Install system dependencies (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            libssl-dev \
            libxdo-dev \
            libfuse3-dev \
            fuse3 \
            pkg-config \
            build-essential
          sudo modprobe fuse || true

      - name: Install WinFsp (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $out = "winfsp.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","$out","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow
          # Verify WinFsp installed and add bin to PATH for DLL discovery
          $winfspDir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
          if ($winfspDir) {
            Write-Host "WinFsp installed at: $winfspDir"
            $binDir = Join-Path $winfspDir "bin"
            Write-Host "Adding to PATH: $binDir"
            echo "$binDir" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append
          } else {
            Write-Host "WARNING: WinFsp registry key not found after install"
          }

      # --- Setup Node.js + pnpm (needed for frontend build before cargo) ---

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # --- Build desktop frontend (Tauri embeds from frontendDist) ---

      - name: Build desktop frontend
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          cd apps/desktop
          pnpm vite build
        env:
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only

      # --- Build debug binary ---

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: ${{ matrix.platform }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: ${{ matrix.platform }}-cargo-

      - name: Create WinFsp MSI placeholder for resource glob (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: powershell
        run: New-Item -ItemType File -Force -Path "apps/desktop/src-tauri/resources/winfsp-placeholder.msi"

      - name: Build debug binary
        run: cargo build --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --features ${{ matrix.fuse-feature }}
        env:
          PKG_CONFIG_PATH: /opt/homebrew/lib/pkgconfig:/usr/local/lib/pkgconfig

      - name: Fix rpath for FUSE-T (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: install_name_tool -add_rpath /usr/local/lib apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/${{ matrix.binary-name }} || true

      # --- Install backend services ---

      - name: Setup PostgreSQL
        uses: ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8
        with:
          username: postgres
          password: postgres
          database: cipherbox_test
          postgres-version: '16'
        id: postgres

      - name: Install Kubo (IPFS) (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install kubo
          ipfs init
          ipfs daemon &
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "IPFS daemon ready"
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

      - name: Install Kubo (IPFS) (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          KUBO_VERSION="v0.34.0"
          curl -fsSL "https://dist.ipfs.tech/kubo/${KUBO_VERSION}/kubo_${KUBO_VERSION}_linux-amd64.tar.gz" | tar -xz
          sudo ./kubo/install.sh
          ipfs init
          ipfs daemon &
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "IPFS daemon ready"
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

      - name: Install Kubo (IPFS) (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          KUBO_VERSION="v0.34.0"
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 \
            "https://dist.ipfs.tech/kubo/${KUBO_VERSION}/kubo_${KUBO_VERSION}_windows-amd64.zip" \
            -o kubo.zip
          unzip -q kubo.zip
          echo "$PWD/kubo" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$PWD/kubo:$PATH"
          ipfs init
          ipfs daemon &
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "IPFS daemon ready"
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

      - name: Install Redis (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install redis
          brew services start redis

      - name: Install Redis (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y redis-server
          sudo systemctl start redis-server

      - name: Install Redis (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          choco install memurai-developer -y --no-progress
          # Memurai installs as a Windows service and starts automatically
          $svc = Get-Service -Name "Memurai" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
          if ($svc -and $svc.Status -eq "Running") {
            Write-Host "Memurai service is running"
          } else {
            # Fallback: start service manually
            Start-Service -Name "Memurai" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
          }
          # Verify Redis is responding
          $env:PATH = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", "Machine") + ";" + $env:PATH
          $ready = $false
          for ($i = 0; $i -lt 10; $i++) {
            try {
              $result = & redis-cli ping 2>$null
              if ($result -eq "PONG") { $ready = $true; break }
            } catch {}
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
          }
          if ($ready) { Write-Host "Redis (Memurai) ready" } else { Write-Host "WARNING: Redis may not be ready" }

      # --- Build backend packages ---

      - name: Build mock-ipns-routing
        run: cd tools/mock-ipns-routing && npm install && npm run build

      - name: Build API
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build

      # --- Configuration ---

      - name: Create API .env
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cat > apps/api/.env << 'ENVEOF'
          NODE_ENV=test
          DB_HOST=localhost
          DB_PORT=5432
          DB_USERNAME=postgres
          DB_PASSWORD=postgres
          DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_test
          JWT_SECRET=e2e-desktop-jwt-secret-key
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:1420
          IPFS_PROVIDER=local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL=http://localhost:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8080
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001
          REDIS_HOST=localhost
          REDIS_PORT=6379
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          ENVEOF
          echo "IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}" >> apps/api/.env

      - name: Create desktop .env
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cat > apps/desktop/.env << 'ENVEOF'
          VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          ENVEOF

      # --- Database + API startup ---

      - name: Run migrations
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
        env:
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
          NODE_ENV: test

      - name: Start mock IPNS routing
        shell: bash
        run: node tools/mock-ipns-routing/dist/index.js &

      - name: Start API server
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          cd apps/api
          node dist/main.js &
          # Wait for API readiness
          READY=0
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -s http://localhost:3000/health > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "API ready"
              READY=1
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$READY" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "API did not become ready in time." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
        env:
          NODE_ENV: test
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
          JWT_SECRET: e2e-desktop-jwt-secret-key
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:1420
          IPFS_PROVIDER: local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL: http://localhost:8080
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL: http://localhost:3001
          REDIS_HOST: localhost
          REDIS_PORT: 6379
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Start API server (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd apps/api
          node dist/main.js &
          # Wait for API readiness
          READY=0
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -s http://localhost:3000/health > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "API ready"
              READY=1
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$READY" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "API did not become ready in time." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
        env:
          NODE_ENV: test
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
          JWT_SECRET: e2e-desktop-jwt-secret-key
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:1420
          IPFS_PROVIDER: local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL: http://localhost:8080
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL: http://localhost:3001
          REDIS_HOST: localhost
          REDIS_PORT: 6379
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      # --- Desktop launch + test execution ---

      - name: Start frontend dev server
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          cd apps/desktop
          pnpm vite preview --port 1420 &
          # Wait for dev server
          for i in $(seq 1 15); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:1420 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Frontend dev server ready on :1420"
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
        env:
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only

      - name: Run desktop E2E tests (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          export CIPHERBOX_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
          export VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
          export VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          export RUST_LOG=info
          BINARY=apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/${{ matrix.binary-name }}
          chmod +x "$BINARY"
          DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
          "$BINARY" --dev-key $DEV_KEY > /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>&1 &
          DESKTOP_PID=$!
          set +e
          bash tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/run-all.sh
          TEST_EXIT=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$TEST_EXIT" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "=== Desktop binary log ==="
            cat /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log file)"
          fi
          kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          diskutil unmount force $HOME/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $TEST_EXIT

      - name: Run desktop E2E tests (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        env:
          CIPHERBOX_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          RUST_LOG: info
          DISPLAY: ':99'
          WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER: '1'
        run: |
          Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1024x768x24 &
          sleep 1
          BINARY=apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/${{ matrix.binary-name }}
          chmod +x "$BINARY"
          DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
          "$BINARY" --dev-key $DEV_KEY > /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>&1 &
          DESKTOP_PID=$!
          set +e
          bash tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/run-all.sh
          TEST_EXIT=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$TEST_EXIT" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "=== Desktop binary log ==="
            cat /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log file)"
          fi
          kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          fusermount3 -u $HOME/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $TEST_EXIT

      - name: Start frontend dev server (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd apps/desktop
          npx vite preview --port 1420 &
          for i in $(seq 1 15); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:1420 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Frontend dev server ready on :1420"
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
        env:
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only

      - name: Run desktop E2E tests (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          BINARY="apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/${{ matrix.binary-name }}"
          DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
          LOGFILE="$RUNNER_TEMP/cipherbox-desktop.log"
          export DESKTOP_LOG="$LOGFILE"
          "$BINARY" --dev-key "$DEV_KEY" > "$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
          DESKTOP_PID=$!
          set +e
          powershell -File "$PWD/tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/run-all.ps1"
          TEST_EXIT=$?
          set -e
          echo "=== Desktop binary log ==="
          cat "$LOGFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log file)"
          kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $TEST_EXIT
        env:
          CIPHERBOX_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          RUST_LOG: info

      # --- Failure artifacts ---

      - name: Upload logs on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-desktop-logs-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: |
            apps/api/*.log
            ~/Library/Logs/fuse-t/fuse-t.log
            /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log
            ${{ runner.temp }}/cipherbox-desktop.log
          retention-days: 7

content.text:
This is a first-release issue. The config is set up correctly for independent versioning — each package is a separate `component` with its own entry in the manifest and `include-component-in-tag: true` (so they get tags like `@cipherbox/core-v0.25.0`).

The reason they're all bumping together in PR #298 is that the single PR #296 touched all packages simultaneously (it created them all). Release Please attributes that commit to every package it changed, so they all get the same `feat` bump.

Going forward, a commit that only touches `packages/sdk/` will only bump `@cipherbox/sdk`, a commit only in `packages/core/` will only bump `@cipherbox/core`, etc. They'll diverge naturally as changes are made independently.

The root package (`.`) also bumped because `apps/web` and `apps/api` changes are attributed to it, and its `extra-files` list propagates the root version to `apps/*/package.json` and `packages/crypto/package.json` — but the four new packages are **not** in that `extra-files` list, so they'll version independently.

content.text:
The workflow config looks fine. The issue is that `pull-request-title-pattern` only controls the **root component's** title pattern. When release-please has a **multi-component** manifest (like yours with 5 packages), it creates a single PR for all components and uses the `target-branch` name ("main") as the title suffix instead of a single version — because there's no single version to show.

The fix is to set `pull-request-title-pattern` at the **top level** of the config (outside `packages`), or adjust the pattern to not use `${version}` since it's ambiguous with multiple components. For example:

```json
"pull-request-title-pattern": "chore: release"
```

Or if you want it to say something more specific:

```json
"pull-request-title-pattern": "chore: release ${branch}"
```

Want me to update it, or do you have a preferred title format?

content.text:
This isn't the build failure anymore — the build is passing now. These are **E2E test failures** at runtime. The key error is:

```
Error: Upload failed with alert: Folder not loaded
```

This is the `ensureFolderRegistered` guard we added — it's now silently skipping registration of folders that aren't fully loaded, so when the upload tries to use the SDK, the folder isn't registered.

content.content:
59→/**
    60→ * Ensure a folder from the Zustand store is registered in the SDK's
    61→ * internal FolderTree. This bridges the gap between folder navigation
    62→ * (which loads folders into Zustand) and SDK operations (which require
    63→ * folders in the SDK's internal state).
    64→ *
    65→ * Only registers if the SDK doesn't already have the folder. The SDK's
    66→ * internal state (sequence number, children, keys) is authoritative once
    67→ * a folder is registered — all mutations go through the SDK.
    68→ */
    69→export function ensureFolderRegistered(folder: FolderNode): void {
    70→  const client = getSdkClient();
    71→
    72→  // Don't overwrite if SDK already has this folder — its internal state
    73→  // is authoritative (correct sequence number, keys, children from mutations)
    74→  if (client.hasFolder(folder.ipnsName)) return;
    75→
    76→  // Guard: don't register placeholder folders that haven't loaded yet —
    77→  // empty key material would cause crypto/IPNS errors on subsequent mutations
    78→  if (!folder.isLoaded || folder.folderKey.length === 0 || folder.ipnsPrivateKey.length === 0) {
    79→    return;
    80→  }
    81→
    82→  client.registerFolder(
    83→    folder.ipnsName,
    84→    folder.folderKey,
    85→    {
    86→      publicKey: new Uint8Array(0), // Public key derived from private key when needed
    87→      privateKey: folder.ipnsPrivateKey,
    88→    },
    89→    folder.children,
    90→    folder.sequenceNumber
    91→  );
    92→}
    93→

content.text: Let me check where `ensureFolderRegistered` is called to understand the timing:

The problem is that by the time `ensureFolderRegistered` is called in the mutation hooks, the folder **is** loaded (it has keys and children). The `isLoaded` check is too strict — the folder store may have a folder that was loaded via navigation (has all keys) but `isLoaded` could be false in an edge case, or the folder may have been loaded by the SDK itself (via `createFolder`) and never set `isLoaded` in the Zustand store.

Let me check what `isLoaded` actually means in the calling context:

The issue is clear. When `ensureFolderRegistered` silently returns without registering (because of the guard), the subsequent `client.createFolder()` throws "Parent folder not loaded" → which surfaces as "Folder not loaded" in the UI. The guard should only check for empty key material, not `isLoaded` — by the time mutations run, the folder has valid keys even if `isLoaded` hasn't been set in every code path.

content.text:
PR #301: https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/301

The root cause: the `isLoaded` flag we added to the guard (from the Copilot review comment) isn't set in all code paths — SDK-created folders and the root folder after vault init have valid keys but `isLoaded` may be false. The guard silently returned without registering, so every subsequent mutation hit "Folder not loaded". Removed the `isLoaded` check, keeping only the empty key material check which is the actual safety condition.

It's the session restore after `page.reload()` — hitting the 360s timeout at the `waitForFunction` checking for vault readiness (line 557). The browser/context was closed (likely by Playwright's test timeout), so the Zustand stores never came back.

94 passed, only test 3.7 failed, and it timed out at the full 360s. This is a CI-specific flakiness issue — the Core Kit session restore on Sapphire Devnet is sometimes extremely slow or fails entirely on CI runners.

This isn't related to the `ensureFolderRegistered` fix. It's the pre-existing reload flakiness on CI. The "Folder not loaded" errors from before are gone (94 tests passed vs 6 failing previously).

Want me to look into making 3.7 more resilient, or is this a known flaky test you're OK retrying?

The `UserMenu` is always rendered in `AppHeader`. The `AppHeader` is shown on authenticated routes. So the user-menu being visible means the app has rendered the authenticated layout — which implies `isAuthenticated` is true. But if `isAuthenticated` is true, then `setAuthenticated()` ran, which means `initializeOrLoadVaultRef` completed. So the vault _should_ have `rootFolderKey` at that point.

Unless there's a race where the Zustand stores haven't exposed themselves to `window.__ZUSTAND_STORES` yet. Let me check:

This is behind `import.meta.env.DEV` — but CI runs a production build (`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build`), not dev mode. So `__ZUSTAND_STORES` **is never set** in the CI build.

That's the root cause. The `waitForFunction` checking `window.__ZUSTAND_STORES?.vault` will **never** succeed in CI because the stores are only exposed in dev mode. The old test flow didn't need this check — it used `reinjectTestAuthAfterReload` instead.

The fix: either expose `__ZUSTAND_STORES` in all environments (or behind a test flag), or change the E2E test to not rely on Zustand store internals and instead wait for a visible UI indicator that vault is ready.

Multiple E2E tests depend on them (conflict-detection, multi-account-wallet, sharing-workflow, full-workflow).

- [ ] E2E test 3.7 (page reload) passes — vault readiness check can now find `__ZUSTAND_STORES`
- [ ] Other E2E tests using `__ZUSTAND_STORES` (conflict-detection, sharing-workflow) pass

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

Now I have all the context. Let me analyze each `__ZUSTAND_STORES` usage systematically:

## Summary Report: `__ZUSTAND_STORES` Usage Analysis

### 1. **conflict-detection.spec.ts, Line 82**
**Context:** In `beforeAll` hook after wallet login
```
Stores accessed:
  - auth.getState().accessToken
  - vault.getState().rootIpnsName

Purpose:
  - Extract access token and root IPNS name to pass to bumpServerSequence() 
    API helper function which simulates another device publishing (bumps server sequence)

Usage:
  - Both values are used to make direct HTTP API calls to trigger conflicts
  - accessToken authorizes the conflict helper request
  - rootIpnsName identifies which IPNS record to bump on server

Could be replaced by UI approach:
  - NO. The whole point is to simulate *server-side* state change without 
    the client knowing about it. This requires direct API access outside 
    the normal UI flow. There's no visual way to observe "server sequence 
    was bumped" — you can only know by trying to publish and getting a 409.
```

### 2. **conflict-detection.spec.ts, Lines 151 & 166**
**Context:** Two helper functions `getAccessToken()` and `getRootIpnsName()`
```
Stores accessed:
  - auth.getState().accessToken
  - vault.getState().rootIpnsName

Purpose:
  - Refresh the token before each test (tokens may be refreshed between tests)
  - Get fresh IPNS name in case it changed
  - Used in the same bumpServerSequence() calls as line 82

Usage:
  - Called once per test that does conflict injection
  - Allows per-test token refresh (testable race conditions)

Could be replaced by UI approach:
  - NO. Same reasoning as line 82 — requires direct API calls that 
    are intentionally outside the normal UI flow.
```

### 3. **full-workflow.spec.ts, Line 564**
**Context:** In test `3.7 Page reload preserves session`, waiting for SDK initialization
```
Stores accessed:
  - vault.getState().rootFolderKey
  - vault.getState().rootIpnsKeypair
  - vault.getState().rootIpnsName

Purpose:
  - Poll for vault initialization to complete after page reload
  - These three fields indicate that initializeOrLoadVault() finished and 
    SDK client is ready for file operations

Usage:
  - page.waitForFunction() that reads Zustand directly (no UI indicator)
  - Required because SDK init can take 10-60s on staging, and there's 
    no visual indicator when it completes

Could be replaced by UI approach:
  - MAYBE. The test could instead wait for "first file to appear" or 
    "file list to become interactive" rather than polling internal state. 
    BUT the current approach is more precise — it waits specifically for 
    crypto keys to be loaded, not just for the list to render (which might 
    be stale/empty). A UI wait would be more fragile if the vault is empty 
    (no items to wait for) or if IPNS resolution is very slow (file list 
    renders empty then gets populated).
    VERDICT: COULD migrate to UI, but current approach is more robust.
```

### 4. **recycle-bin.spec.ts, Lines 48 & 369**
**Context:** Line 48 is a helper type definition; Line 369 is in test `TC07` reading quota
```
Stores accessed:
  - quota.getState().usedBytes

Purpose:
  - Read storage quota used bytes from Zustand quota store
  - Check that permanent delete actually reclaimed storage
  - This is a "best-effort" check with fallback (returns null if store not exposed)

Usage:
  - Line 48: Defines a helper function getQuotaUsedBytes() that safely tries 
    to read quota, catches errors, returns null
  - Line 369: Called to snapshot quota before/after permanent delete operations
  - The test passes even if quota store isn't accessible (not a hard assertion)

Could be replaced by UI approach:
  - MAYBE. The storage quota IS displayed in the UI ("[data-testid="storage-quota"]") 
    and was already tested in full-workflow.spec.ts tests 3.6.1 and 3.7.1 
    using getComputedStyle. The Zustand approach is just more direct/precise. 
    The test explicitly documents this as "best-effort" with fallback.
    VERDICT: COULD migrate to reading computed style of quota display, but 
    would be more brittle if quota element doesn't update immediately after unpin.
```

### 5. **multi-account-wallet.ts, Line 34**
**Context:** In helper function `extractAuthState()` called after wallet login
```
Stores accessed:
  - auth.getState().accessToken
  - auth.getState().vaultKeypair?.publicKey
  - vault.getState().rootIpnsName

Purpose:
  - Extract auth state to populate WalletTestAccount interface
  - publicKey is used for sharing (file sharing between accounts)
  - accessToken is used for direct API calls
  - rootIpnsName is used for conflict detection API calls

Usage:
  - Called once per test account after wallet login
  - Returned values stored in account object for entire test
  - publicKey, accessToken, rootIpnsName later used to make direct API calls 
    in multi-account sharing tests

Could be replaced by UI approach:
  - NO. These fields are specifically needed for programmatic API calls 
    (sharing, conflict detection) that happen outside the normal UI flow. 
    There's no way to "visually extract" a public key or access token.
```

### 6. **wallet-login-helpers.ts, Line 166**
**Context:** In `loginViaWallet()` function, waiting for vault init after successful login
```
Stores accessed:
  - vault.getState().rootFolderKey
  - vault.getState().rootIpnsKeypair
  - vault.getState().rootIpnsName

Purpose:
  - Same as full-workflow.spec.ts line 564
  - Poll for vault init to complete before returning from login function
  - Prevents race condition where test tries file operations before SDK ready

Usage:
  - page.waitForFunction() that reads Zustand
  - Called in every test that does wallet login
  - Without this, tests would race with async vault initialization

Could be replaced by UI approach:
  - MAYBE. Could wait for file list to render instead. But this is the 
    "canonical" way to detect SDK readiness (crypto keys loaded), not just 
    UI rendering. Same tradeoff as #3.
    VERDICT: COULD migrate, but less precise.
```

### 7. **web3auth-helpers.ts, Lines 233 & 242**
**Context:** In `injectAuthState()` function, waiting for stores to be exposed
```
Line 233:
  - Accesses: window.__ZUSTAND_STORES (checking if it exists)
  - Purpose: Verify stores are exposed before injecting state
  - Not reading store content, just checking it exists

Line 242:
  - Accesses: auth store's setState() and vault store's getState().setVaultKeys()
  - Purpose: Inject TestAuthState into stores after test-login
  - Writes to stores (not just reading)

Usage:
  - Line 232-237: Waits for stores to exist (timeout 15s) before proceeding
  - Line 241-267: Injects auth + vault state into stores to simulate login 
    without Core Kit (test-login endpoint bypass)

Could be replaced by UI approach:
  - NO. This is injecting internal state for test infrastructure, not reading it. 
    There's no UI action that would inject raw auth state into Zustand. 
    This is pure test scaffolding.
```

---

## Summary Table

| File | Line(s) | Stores | Purpose | UI Alternative? |
|------|---------|--------|---------|-----------------|
| conflict-detection.spec.ts | 82 | auth.accessToken, vault.rootIpnsName | Conflict injection via API | ❌ No (requires API) |
| conflict-detection.spec.ts | 151, 166 | auth.accessToken, vault.rootIpnsName | Token refresh + conflict API | ❌ No (requires API) |
| full-workflow.spec.ts | 564 | vault.rootFolderKey, rootIpnsKeypair, rootIpnsName | Poll for SDK init | ⚠️ Maybe (less precise) |
| recycle-bin.spec.ts | 48, 369 | quota.usedBytes | Check storage reclaim | ⚠️ Maybe (less direct) |
| multi-account-wallet.ts | 34 | auth.accessToken, auth.vaultKeypair, vault.rootIpnsName | Extract for sharing/conflict API | ❌ No (requires API) |
| wallet-login-helpers.ts | 166 | vault.rootFolderKey, rootIpnsKeypair, rootIpnsName | Poll for SDK init | ⚠️ Maybe (less precise) |
| web3auth-helpers.ts | 233, 242 | __ZUSTAND_STORES (check existence & inject) | Test infrastructure/state injection | ❌ No (infrastructure) |

**Key Finding:** 5/7 usages **cannot** be replaced by UI approaches because they:
1. Make **direct API calls outside the normal UI flow** (conflict injection, sharing)
2. **Inject test infrastructure state** (state injection for test-login bypass)

Only **2/7 usages** (SDK init polling) could potentially migrate to UI waits, but would lose precision and become more fragile.

content: why can the sharing tests not use the existing ui elements rather?

content.text:
Here's the breakdown:

**Can't eliminate store access (5 of 7 usages):**
- **conflict-detection** & **multi-account-wallet** — need `accessToken` and `rootIpnsName` to make direct API calls outside the UI (conflict injection, sharing). No visual equivalent.
- **web3auth-helpers** — *writes* to stores to inject test state. Pure infrastructure.

**Could use UI instead (2 of 7):**
- **full-workflow test 3.7** — polls vault for `rootFolderKey`. Could just wait for the file list to appear instead (which already happens on the next line).
- **wallet-login-helpers** — same vault readiness poll after login. Could wait for the file list/empty state instead (which the caller already does).

So realistically, store exposure is necessary — the sharing and conflict tests need raw tokens and IPNS names for direct API calls. But we can eliminate the two "vault readiness" polls and replace them with UI waits.

The immediate fix is still to expose `__ZUSTAND_STORES` in production builds since those API-driven tests genuinely need it. Want me to:

1. Keep the PR as-is (expose stores in all builds), or
2. Do a hybrid — expose stores in all builds for the API tests, but also replace the two vault readiness polls with UI waits so they don't depend on it?

content.text:
The public key is displayed on the Settings page in `.settings-pubkey-value`. So for each test account, instead of extracting from Zustand, the test could:

1. Navigate to `/settings`
2. Read the text from `.settings-pubkey-value`
3. Navigate back to `/files`

Now let me check the conflict-detection tests — those need `accessToken` and `rootIpnsName`:

The conflict tests need `accessToken` for API auth and `rootIpnsName` to identify which record to bump. The `rootIpnsName` isn't displayed anywhere in the UI. And `accessToken` is an HTTP-only internal value.

However — could the conflict test call the bump API *through the browser* instead of directly? Using `page.evaluate` to make a fetch from the browser context (which would include cookies automatically)?

So here's the full picture:

**Sharing tests** — only need `publicKey`, which **is visible in the UI** on the Settings page. These could absolutely navigate to Settings, read the key from `.settings-pubkey-value`, and navigate back. No Zustand access needed.

**Conflict detection tests** — need `accessToken` and `rootIpnsName` to call a server API that simulates another device. These are inherently non-UI operations. But even these could potentially use `page.evaluate(() => fetch(...))` from the browser context (cookies auto-included) instead of needing the raw token. The `rootIpnsName` is the harder one — it's not displayed in the UI anywhere.

**Vault readiness polls** — completely replaceable with UI waits (file list appearing).

So the answer is: yes, the sharing tests absolutely could use the Settings page UI to get the public key. The only tests that truly need store access are:
- Conflict detection (needs `rootIpnsName` which isn't in the UI)
- The `web3auth-helpers` state injection (test infrastructure)

Want me to refactor the sharing/multi-account flow to extract the public key from the Settings page UI instead?

Exactly. The full-workflow tests run as `test.describe.serial` — when 3.7 fails, all 36 subsequent tests are skipped. And the conflict-detection, sharing-workflow, and other spec files that use `__ZUSTAND_STORES` also fail in the same run but we've been focused on 3.7 as the first failure.

Looking back at the failing run output:

```
6 failed
94 passed
36 did not run
```

Those 6 failures likely include conflict-detection and sharing-workflow hitting the same `__ZUSTAND_STORES` issue. The fix needs to cover all of them, not just 3.7.

So the plan should be:
1. **Expose `__ZUSTAND_STORES` in all builds** — needed for conflict-detection (`rootIpnsName`) and web3auth-helpers (state injection)
2. **Replace vault readiness polls** (full-workflow 3.7, wallet-login-helpers) with UI waits
3. **Extract public keys from Settings UI** in sharing/multi-account tests instead of from Zustand

Want me to tackle all three, or start with just #1 (the minimal fix) to unblock CI?

```typescript
if (import.meta.env.DEV || import.meta.env.VITE_E2E) {
```

The CI workflow already passes env vars to the web build step:

```yaml
- name: Build packages (excluding desktop)
  run: |
    ...
    pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build
  env:
    VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
    VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
    # just add:
    VITE_E2E: true
```

Vite bakes `VITE_*` env vars into the build at compile time, so it gets tree-shaken out of production deploys (where `VITE_E2E` isn't set). Want me to implement this?

name: E2E Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to checkout (tag, branch, or SHA)'
        required: false
        type: string

jobs:
  e2e:
    name: E2E Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.34.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}

      - name: Setup pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/e2e exec playwright install chromium --with-deps

      - name: Install mock-ipns-routing dependencies
        run: |
          cd tools/mock-ipns-routing
          npm install
          npm run build

      - name: Build packages (excluding desktop)
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build
        env:
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000

      - name: Create .env files for E2E
        run: |
          # Web app .env (for Vite dev server)
          echo "VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}" > apps/web/.env
          echo "VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000" >> apps/web/.env
          # API .env (for NestJS)
          echo "NODE_ENV=test" > apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_HOST=localhost" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_PORT=5432" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_USERNAME=postgres" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_PASSWORD=postgres" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_test" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "JWT_SECRET=e2e-test-jwt-secret-key-for-ci" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IPFS_PROVIDER=local" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL=http://localhost:5001" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8080" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "REDIS_HOST=localhost" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "REDIS_PORT=6379" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only" >> apps/api/.env
          echo "IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}" >> apps/api/.env

      - name: Run E2E tests
        # Run all tests in the tests/ directory (archived tests live in tests/archive/)
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/e2e test
        env:
          CI: true
          # Database configuration
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
          NODE_ENV: test
          # IPFS configuration
          IPFS_PROVIDER: local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL: http://localhost:8080
          # API configuration
          JWT_SECRET: e2e-test-jwt-secret-key-for-ci
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: http://localhost:5173
          # IPNS delegated routing (mock service for E2E tests)
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL: http://localhost:3001
          # Redis for BullMQ job scheduling
          REDIS_HOST: localhost
          REDIS_PORT: 6379
          # Web app configuration (needed for Web3Auth initialization)
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          # Test-login endpoint for E2E (bypasses Core Kit, uses deterministic keypair)
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          # Web3Auth test credentials (fallback if TEST_LOGIN_SECRET not set)
          WEB3AUTH_TEST_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.WEB3AUTH_TEST_EMAIL }}
          WEB3AUTH_TEST_OTP: ${{ secrets.WEB3AUTH_TEST_OTP }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: |
            tests/e2e/playwright-report/
            tests/e2e/test-results/
          retention-days: 7
